title: Security milestone chronograph and owner rotation protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a prescriptive, time-boxed milestone chronograph and owner-rotation protocol for all major assurance initiatives (SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, audit logs). The chronograph is a lightweight schedule + accountability matrix that: 1) reduces single-point-of-failure ownership, 2) ensures evidence producers rotate predictably, and 3) standardizes sprint handoffs between PM, Eng, Design, and Security.

Scope: Deliver a playbook (runbook) and a corresponding dashboard template that programs: milestone cadence, handoff triggers (e.g., evidence ready, audit window start), owner rotation rules, escalation steps, and automated reminders. This work covers: runbook authoring, dashboard template in Console, Slack reminder automation, and a short training session for assurance leads.

Out-of-scope: Changes to the primary audit evidence schema or identity provider configurations (those are tracked in separate ENG/SEC tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Published runbook in Confluence with step-by-step handoff checklist and owner rotation policy
Dashboard template created in Console showing milestone state, owner schedule, and outstanding evidence buckets
Automation configured: Slack reminders for handoff + 48/24/0 hour alerts and an optional calendar invite generator
Two cross-functional dry runs executed with artifact capture and retrospective notes
Documented rollback/escalation play for missed evidence windows
milestones: M1: Runbook draft and policy sign-off by Security & PM (2025-02-26)
M2: Console dashboard template and data connectors (2025-03-10)
M3: Slack automation + calendar invite generator (2025-03-18)
M4: Two dry-run rehearsals with OSS & Enterprise teams (2025-03-28)
M5: Finalize runbook, publish, and training session (2025-04-08)
timeline: High-level timeline spans Feb 12 -> Apr 15. Front-load policy work and sign-offs, then progressively deliver dashboard + automation, ending with dry runs and training. Critical path: Security sign-off (M1) -> Data connector availability (M2) -> Dry-run coordination (M4).
risks: Delay in data ingest for dashboard (depends on ENG backlog)
Ambiguity in who qualifies as ‘evidence owner’ across orgs
Insufficient attendance for dry-run rehearsals leading to shallow feedback
Automation tokens / secrets approvals slow down Slack/calendar integration
mitigations: Escalate data ingest dependency to infra sync (ENG-1842) and reserve a 2-day buffer
Add a one-page evidence-owner definition in the runbook with examples by product area
Schedule dry-runs 3 weeks in advance and include mandatory invite for assurance leads
Coordinate with Security on SCIM/KMS gating early; request temporary sandbox tokens for dev
